title: What the blues means to her; "Adam and Eve Had the Blues"
summary: Wallace says the blues is anything miserable, mentions songs written with her brother, and plays a song she completed herself.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the blues is, and why every jazz player needs it

blocks.x: You remember. Okay, good, Very good. I'd like to ask you, what the blues means to you, Ms. Wallace?
Let me tell you, I've been mistreated in my life. I tell you how I've been mistreated. (Inaudible) I don't know what some people think but the blues is anything

anything that is miserable to you, you know. And now I (unintelligible) my brother, we worked (unintelligible). Me and Buddy was writing our songs before Mama died. And I know my brother would cry. Nobody could ever forget that song (unintelligible). I couldn't get together while my brother was living but I got together now, I'll tell you.
"Adam and Eve Had the Blues." And you got it together yourself?
That's lovely. Beautiful. Do you think there could be such a thing as happy blues?

Well, sometimes if something happen that you wanted to be -- telling people what you want (unintelligible). But most times when people get the blues, it's something like they don't (unintelligible). Some people ain't going to call it the blues, I said, but honey, I said, blues are. Blues are. (Unintelligible).
